national_posture.statement: The United States was at National Preparedness Level 5; the 0730 MDT IMSR listed 94 uncontained large fires, 133 active incidents, and 28,700 assigned personnel.
national_posture.level_meaning: national resources are fully committed, active geographic areas may need emergency measures, and potential for additional significant fires is high

national_posture.statement: CWFIS listed 687 active fires, 4,486 fires year to date, and 9,529,813 acres (3,856,579 hectares) burned year to date for August 5; CIFFC's 4:20 PM EDT report placed Canada at National Preparedness Level 5 and British Columbia at agency preparedness level 5, with extreme national resource demand and international resources mobilizing.
national_posture.level_meaning: national demand is extreme, Canadian resources are fully committed, and international resources are being mobilized to sustain operations

incidents.name: Old Trails Fire
incidents.location: West of Spokane near Airway Heights

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road, trail, and area closures remained in effect around the fire.

incidents.operational_outlook: The controlling incident page described moderate flanking and backing, persistent heat in structure debris, continued structure protection and mop-up, and little to no expected perimeter growth before warmer and drier conditions.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage combines the first-degree arson charge and personal-loss accounts with the afternoon operational improvement to 13% containment across Old Trails.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 77 items from 49 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours; the seven-day query hit the 100-item display cap, so the 14.3-item daily baseline is a lower bound and the 5.4-times acceleration is an upper bound; RSS returned no usable items, and no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The IMSR's 570 losses are unspecified structures, so they should not be converted into a dwelling count without parcel-level assessment. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Bradley Creek Fire
incidents.location: Okanagan Indian Band reserve near Vernon

evacuation.description: Okanagan Indian Band members were evacuated with very short lead time as the fire entered the reserve community.

incidents.operational_outlook: BC Wildfire Service continued to classify Bradley Creek FSR as out of control and showed four evacuation orders and three evacuation alerts from the Okanagan Indian Band and neighboring jurisdictions.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage centers on the preliminary estimate of about 230 homes destroyed in the Okanagan Indian Band community, residents escaping with only minutes of notice, and aerial drops that helped protect a daycare and school.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 49 items from 27 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 75 items in the seven-day query, a 10.7-item daily baseline and 4.6-times acceleration; RSS returned no usable items, and no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** CIFFC's August 5 priority table now lists Bradley Creek separately at 2,852 hectares, matching the exact BCWS K41351 page. ([BC Wildfire Service](https://wildfiresituation.nrs.gov.bc.ca/incidents?fireYear=2026&incidentNumber=K41351); [CIFFC](https://ciffc.net/situation/)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The roughly 230-home estimate is the strongest new residential-loss signal in Canada today, but it remains a preliminary estimate from the Okanagan Indian Band chief rather than a completed parcel-level damage assessment. ([Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/wildfire-canada-homes-destroyed-british-columbia-fbbb7f027adb04a9c9b47a109de74082))
critical_alert_reasons: at least 25 newly damaged or destroyed structures
named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Autumn Lane Fire
incidents.location: Spokane and Stevens counties near Suncrest and Nine Mile Falls

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road and trail closures remained in effect, including Level 3 zones around Suncrest and Nine Mile Falls.

incidents.operational_outlook: The controlling incident page described moderate fire behavior and continuing aggressive structure protection in the wildland-urban interface, with critically dry fuels expected to remain active after the morning inversion lifted.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasizes the afternoon gain to 13% containment, crews holding fire lines, and continuing evacuation and access constraints around Suncrest and Nine Mile Falls.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 41 items from 25 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 85 items in the seven-day query, a 12.1-item daily baseline and 3.4-times acceleration; RSS returned no usable items, and no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 80 losses are an unspecified-structure total, while the continued threat is explicitly residential; keep realized loss and residential exposure as separate fields. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Fairview Fire

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road, trail, and area closures remained in effect near Mead.

incidents.operational_outlook: The controlling incident page described moderate backing, creeping, and smoldering, persistent heat in structure debris, continued structure protection and mop-up, and little to no expected perimeter growth.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage treats Fairview as part of the wider Spokane disaster while highlighting the first measurable containment gain to 5%; no new Fairview-specific loss count was reported.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 32 items from 23 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 85 items in the seven-day query, a 12.1-item daily baseline and 2.6-times acceleration; it fell below the 40-item High threshold, RSS returned no usable items, and no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 57 losses are unspecified structures and the infrastructure threat is qualitative, so neither should be converted into a residential count or modeled exposure count. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Aspen Acres Fire
incidents.controlling_agency: Rocky Mountain Complex Incident Management Team 3

evacuation.description: Area and road closures remained in effect; the IMSR did not report an active evacuation count.

incidents.operational_outlook: Minimal fire behavior was expected, and command was scheduled to return to a local Type 3 organization on August 5 as resources were released.

attention.coverage_summary: Recent coverage emphasizes improving containment and the release of resources as management transitions back to a local team, framing the fire as moving toward stabilization rather than renewed structural loss.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 22 items from 14 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 72 items in the seven-day query, a 10.3-item daily baseline and 2.1-times acceleration; RSS returned no usable items, and no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** Treat the IMSR's 915 lost structures as a cumulative incident total, not an August 5 damage increment; the report does not split the total into residences, commercial buildings, or outbuildings. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))

incidents.name: Pear Lake Fire
incidents.location: Thompson-Nicola Regional District and Village of Clinton

evacuation.description: BC Wildfire Service showed eight active evacuation orders issued by regional districts, First Nations, and the Village of Clinton, plus four evacuation alerts.

incidents.operational_outlook: Damage assessment was incomplete because some suspected loss areas were not yet safely accessible.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage focuses on the incomplete damage assessment affecting about 120 properties, stressing that losses include garages, sheds, and other outbuildings and should not be read as 120 destroyed dwellings.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 15 items from 10 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 47 items in the seven-day query, a 6.7-item daily baseline and 2.2-times acceleration; RSS returned no usable items, and no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** Do not equate about 120 affected properties with 120 destroyed dwellings: the regional district said some properties lost only garages, sheds, or other outbuildings while the residences remained standing, and assessment was incomplete. ([CTV News](https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/more-than-100-structures-lost-in-bcs-pear-lake-wildfire-officials-say/))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Kaiser Canyon Fire
incidents.controlling_agency: Bureau of Indian Affairs and Alaska Incident Management Team 2

evacuation.description: Evacuations and road and area closures remained in effect south of Nespelem.

incidents.operational_outlook: The controlling incident page described active fire behavior and continued structure protection around Nespelem, Agency, Disautel, Highway 155, and the Highway 21 corridor under a warming and drying trend.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage links Kaiser Canyon's continued burning and active evacuation footprint with the wider North Central Washington fire emergency, emphasizing structure protection and worsening regional conditions.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 15 items from seven title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours versus 53 items in the seven-day query, a 7.6-item daily baseline and 2.0-times acceleration; RSS returned no usable items, and no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The 44 losses are cumulative and unspecified by occupancy class; numerous structures were still threatened, but the IMSR gave no numerical exposure count. ([NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf))
critical_alert_reasons: named community under evacuation with structure involvement or imminent threat

incidents.name: Rowe Creek Complex
incidents.location: South of Fossil across central Oregon counties
incidents.controlling_agency: Pacific Northwest Complex Incident Management Team 3 and Oregon State Fire Marshal

evacuation.description: The official update directed residents to county evacuation maps because zones could change quickly; it did not state a single complex-wide evacuation level.

incidents.operational_outlook: Structural crews continued point protection and triage near developed areas while U.S. Highway 26 remained closed for suppression operations.

attention.coverage_summary: Coverage emphasizes the complex's exceptional scale and improving containment, but recent headlines citing 329,012 acres and 62% differ from the current InciWeb basic-information and IMSR values of 325,265 acres and 57% used here.
attention.methodology_note: The browser-visible Google News query returned 26 items from 18 title-attributed publishers in the preceding 24 hours; the seven-day query hit the 100-item display cap, so the 14.3-item daily baseline is a lower bound and the 1.8-times acceleration is an upper bound. Because the 1.5-times threshold cannot be established from the censored baseline, attention is conservatively Low; RSS returned no usable items and no auditable public-discussion count was available at cutoff.

incidents.analyst_note: **Source reconciliation:** InciWeb's current basic-information fields and the August 5 IMSR both support 325,265 acres and 57% containment; a highlighted InciWeb update and recent coverage carried newer 329,012-acre and 62% figures, so this briefing retains the duplicated controlling values while flagging the same-page conflict. ([InciWeb](https://inciweb.wildfire.gov/incident-information/orprd-rowe-creek-complex); [NIFC IMSR](https://www.nifc.gov/nicc/sitreprt.pdf)) **Cat-modeling interpretation:** The complex-wide 25-loss total is not classified by occupancy, and current updates do not establish a new loss increment.

global_overview.statement: The reviewed international headline sample was concentrated in Europe: the highest-impact events were in Spain and France, active flare-up risk remained in Greece, and new evacuations were reported in Albania; no Australian event reached the same headline threshold at the cutoff. This is a headline scan, not comprehensive worldwide operational intelligence.

global_events.name: Mallakastër and Gjirokastër fires
global_events.status: Ground and aerial crews were actively protecting homes in Mallakastër; a second likely lightning-caused fire remained active in mountainous terrain south of Gjirokastër
global_events.evacuations: About 15 families were evacuated with livestock and pets.
global_events.summary: The Albania events were the newest promoted international fires at the cutoff, but no verified structure-loss or burned-area count was published in the reviewed report.

global_events.name: Porto Germeno and western Attica fires
global_events.status: Several fires west of Athens were largely contained, but hundreds of firefighters remained to prevent flare-ups before stronger winds and hotter temperatures
global_events.evacuations: More than 1,000 people evacuated, including more than 250 rescued by boat; an exact destroyed-home count was not reported.
global_events.summary: Homes and farmland were destroyed around Porto Germeno, but the reviewed source did not provide a defensible structural-loss total.

global_events.name: Bordeaux–Le Porge fire
global_events.status: The fire was contained and thousands of evacuees were returning, but it was not fully extinguished
global_events.evacuations: More than 224,000 people fled during France's largest civilian evacuation outside wartime.
global_events.summary: Fire damage exposed more than 400 suspected World War II shells and other munitions in Le Porge, adding an unusual recovery and access constraint.

global_events.name: Almería fire and central Spain fire complexes
global_events.status: Many July fires were easing or controlled, but recurrent heatwaves were sustaining renewed wildfire risk
global_events.evacuations: More than 1,500 people evacuated during the Almería fire; later fires also displaced residents around Madrid.
global_events.summary: The merged fires near Madrid were estimated at about 172,974–197,684 acres (70,000–80,000 hectares), while a campsite operator reported that about half of its mobile homes burned; no consolidated national structure-loss total was available.

rejected_candidates.name: Sinlahekin Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported rapid growth and two structures lost, but no numeric threatened-structure count; it remained below today's eight-incident structural-impact cutoff.

rejected_candidates.name: Modrite Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported 15 structures lost, 35% containment, evacuations, and qualitative threats, but it remained below the 25-structure promotion threshold and lacked a higher structural signal.

rejected_candidates.name: Bench Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported 13 structures lost and 84% containment; it remained below the 25-structure promotion threshold and showed substantially greater suppression progress than promoted fires.

rejected_candidates.name: Fox Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported eight structures lost and 61% containment, below the structural-impact cutoff for the displayed watchlist.

rejected_candidates.name: Second Flat Fire
rejected_candidates.reason: The IMSR reported seven structures lost and 55% containment, below the structural-impact cutoff for the displayed watchlist.

rejected_candidates.name: Ainslie Creek and Brunswick Creek fires
rejected_candidates.reason: CIFFC listed both as out-of-control British Columbia priority fires, but reviewed sources did not establish qualifying structural loss, a numeric structure threat, or headline momentum comparable with Bradley Creek and Pear Lake.
